**The Getaway Route** is a PSY475 escape-room puzzle on the task-switching paradigm. Players trace a fleeing suspect through a maze while Evidence-ID Audits interrupt at random. Each correct answer adds a digit to the case code.

## Download

| System | File | How to run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows 10/11 (64-bit) | `Getaway-Route-<version>-Windows.exe` | Double-click it. Nothing to install. If SmartScreen says "Windows protected your PC", click **More info**, then **Run anyway** (the app isn't code-signed). |
| macOS 10.15 Catalina or newer (Intel and Apple silicon) | `Getaway-Route-<version>-macOS.dmg` | Open the .dmg and drag **The Getaway Route** to Applications (or run it from the .dmg). The first time, **right-click the app and choose Open**, then **Open** again (the app isn't notarized by Apple). If macOS says the app is damaged, run `xattr -cr "/Applications/The Getaway Route.app"` in Terminal once. |

Press **F11** in the app for full screen.

## What's new since v1.0.1

- **Fixed:** a correct answer could be judged wrong when new exhibits appeared just as it was typed. After a miss, the right exhibit is now highlighted and the answer explained.
- **Each leg is harder:** a bigger maze and one more exhibit per audit every leg.
- **Route-error alarm:** wall hits and doubling back glitch the screen, shake the console, flash the walls red and sound a loud alarm.
- **Back-to-back audits** once you reach the exit early.
- **Charts** on the Case Closed screen: solve time per leg (line) and time per audit (with total played).
- **Esc pauses** the game; the case timer and audit countdown bar now display correctly.

## For facilitators

- Click the **gear** button (bottom right) and enter the access code to change any setting: legs, maze size, audit timing and clock, strikes, practice audits, the Old Case Key, and the Case Closed clue. Settings are saved on that computer.
- **NEW CASE** (or Ctrl+Shift+N) starts a fresh mission for the next group.

See the README for how to play, every setting, and how the puzzle links to task switching.
